---
title: "2. PETPrep"
---

[PETPrep](https://github.com/nipreps/petprep) preprocesses PET data. It corrects for head motion, registers the PET images to the participant's MRI, and extracts time-activity curves (TACs) from FreeSurfer regions. A full run takes hours per participant, so you look at outputs that have already been computed for this dataset.

## 2.1 Part 1: Look at the PETPrep outputs

### The reports

PETPrep writes one HTML report per participant. To open a report, run:

```bash
/neurodesktop-storage/course-material/pet/scripts/view_petprep.sh sub-XX.html # choose a subject
```

The script prints a link. Open it in a new browser tab. When you are done, press Ctrl+C in the terminal. To see a list of all reports, run the script without a filename.

While you look through the reports, think about whether you would accept each step of the pipeline.

### The output files

Explore the outputs in `~/pet_course/derivatives/petprep`. Open one participant's folder. For example, find the TAC file `sub-01_ses-baseline_desc-preproc_seg-gtm_tacs.tsv` and open it in JupyterLab.

(the image files are unfortunately empty to save on disk space)

## 2.2 Part 2: Explore the PETPrep options

Stop when you get here. This exercise is performed with slides, where you will propose which option might resolve the issue.

You don't run PETPrep in this workshop. Instead, you install `petprep-docker`, a Python wrapper that builds the full command to run PETPrep in a container, and you explore its options.

```bash
pip install --user petprep-docker
petprep-docker --help
```

You can ignore the pip warning that `~/.local/bin` isn't on your PATH.

Read through the help text to get an overview of what you can change. In the slides, you then see examples of PETPrep runs that went wrong. For each example, look through the options and work out what you could do differently to make the run work.
